subject: Finly discovery recap - p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap - p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency

Anna —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points & context
- Current infra: Finly routes requests to a mixture of OpenAI hosted endpoints for prototyping and an in-house GPU pool (K8s + Triton) for heavier workloads. You currently see large variance in token latency under load and some poor streaming UX (long gaps during first tokens and jitter mid-stream).
- Business impact: Consumers expect near-real-time streaming in the assistant; current gaps are causing drop-offs during long-form responses. Engineering expects to scale to ~200 concurrent active requests at peak (sustained) and higher burst concurrency.
- Success criteria you called out: p95 end-to-end latency for short completions (<= 200ms), streaming token latency (time-to-first-token <= 100ms and steady token cadence), and support for 150-250 sustained concurrent streams without significant tail latency degradation.

Observed constraints today (from your notes)
- Model: mix of open LLMs and a tuned 13B variant quantized to int8 on A100s.
- Load balancer + prefix caching exists but is per-request and not cross-request; no KV cache for partial prompts.
- Clients: mobile and web with aggressive timeouts; UX degrades if first-token >120ms.

Proposed approach / next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (1.5 hrs) - triage current request flow, sequence lengths, and kernel footprints. Propose Wed 7/16 or Thu 7/17.
2) Pilot config - we suggest a 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated: enable streaming optimizations, prefix KV caching, and continuous batching. Goal: demonstrate p95 improvement and stable streaming cadence under a 72-hour soak.
3) Measurement plan - we'll co-author a short eval checklist (p95 latency, time-to-first-token, tokens/sec during streaming, error rates, cost per 1k tokens).
4) Commercial path - after pilot, scope committed capacity for 3 months with SLA targets and a rollout plan.

Attachments: finly-p95-requirements.pdf (summary of your targets), redline-mpa.docx (initial commercial agreement template).

Thanks - I'll loop in engineering for the deep-dive once you confirm a slot.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap - p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency

Aditya —

Thanks for the concise recap - this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- The 200ms p95 target is for short (<= 256 token) assistant responses called from our web UI. For long responses we care more about steady streaming cadence and avoiding >500ms pauses.
- Concurrency: 150 sustained is the minimum; we should be able to handle 300 bursts for 60-90s windows.
- Current quantized model is running on a small fleet of A100s; we have no automatic fallback to cheaper variants and that is causing throttles during busy hours.

We'll confirm deep-dive availability now - Thu 7/17 10:00 PT works for engineering and product. Please include someone from your runtime team who can speak to KV cache and batching behavior.

Also: can you share any previous streaming benchmarks you have (time-to-first-token numbers) and a short checklist you plan to use for the pilot?

- Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Engineering, Finly
anna.lopez@finly.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap - p95 targets, streaming UX, concurrency

Anna -

Perfect - Thu 7/17 10:00 PT is booked on my side. Invites to follow. I'll have Ravi (runtime lead) join to go over kernel selection, KV cache semantics, and continuous batching.

Quick answers to your asks (and I'll bring detailed slides to the deep-dive):
- Streaming benchmarks: we typically see time-to-first-token in the 40-80ms range for short prompts on Dedicated with optimized kernels and warmed KV caches; p95 tail token gaps (mid-stream) usually below 120ms under well-configured batching. I'll attach a short benchmark packet to the invite.
- Pilot checklist highlights:
  * Measure p95 end-to-end latency (client -> model -> client) for <=256 token responses
  * Measure time-to-first-token for streaming across device types
  * Validate sustained concurrency at 150-250 streams and burst to 300+ for 60-90s
  * Track error rates and fallback behavior (model variant fallback success, 429s, timeouts)
  * Cost estimates for observed token volumes

Attached: finly-p95-requirements.pdf (updated with your concurrency clarifications).

Next steps:
- I'll send calendar invite for Thu 7/17 10:00 PT with a short agenda and attach the benchmark packet + checklist.
- If you want us to run a short smoke test ahead of the deep-dive (sample traffic), tell me which endpoint/keys to hit and we can produce an initial profile.

Looking forward -
Aditya
